title: 行香子·述怀
title_en: Walking with Incense: Telling My Heart
author: 苏轼

text_note.zh: 原始资料只题词牌“行香子”。通行本加题目“述怀”，意思是说说心里话。
text_note.en: The source gives only the tune name, Xingxiangzi. Common editions add the title "Telling My Heart".

readings.en: Read shuí, the usual reading in poems.

readings.zh: 这里是“快乐”的意思，读 lè，不读 yuè。
readings.en: Here it means joy, so it is read lè, not yuè.

glosses.zh: 无尘：没有一点灰尘，形容夜晚干净清爽。
glosses.en: wú chén: not a speck of dust; the night is clean and clear.
zhēn: to pour wine into a cup.

glosses.zh: 须满十分：一定要倒得满满的。十分，十成，全满。
glosses.en: xū mǎn shí fēn: it must be filled right to the top. Shí fēn means ten tenths, completely full.

glosses.zh: 浮名浮利：像水上浮着的东西一样靠不住的名声和钱财。
glosses.en: fú míng fú lì: fame and wealth that float like things on water and cannot be counted on.

glosses.zh: 虚苦劳神：白白受苦，耗费精神。
glosses.en: xū kǔ láo shén: suffering for nothing and wearing out your mind.

glosses.zh: 隙中驹：从墙缝里看一匹白马跑过，一闪就没了。出自《庄子》，比喻时间过得飞快。
glosses.en: xì zhōng jū: a white horse seen running past a crack in a wall, gone in a flash. The image comes from the book Zhuangzi, and means time flies.

glosses.zh: 石中火：用石头敲出的火星，一闪就灭，比喻人生短暂。
glosses.en: shí zhōng huǒ: the spark struck from a flint, gone in an instant; life is short.

glosses.zh: 梦中身：好像活在梦里，比喻人生虚幻。
glosses.en: mèng zhōng shēn: as if living in a dream; life is not as solid as it seems.

glosses.zh: 抱文章：满肚子学问，很有文采。
glosses.en: bào wén zhāng: to be full of learning and good at writing.

glosses.zh: 开口谁亲：说出心里话，又有谁来亲近、理解我呢。
glosses.en: kāi kǒu shuí qīn: when I speak my mind, who will be close to me and understand?
qiě: for now, for the time being.

glosses.zh: 陶陶：快快乐乐、无忧无虑的样子。
天真：人本来的样子，不做作的真性情。
glosses.en: tiān zhēn: one's natural, true self, without pretending.

glosses.zh: 闲人：没有官职、无事一身轻的人。
glosses.en: xián rén: a person with no official job and nothing weighing on him.

glosses.zh: 一溪云：一条小溪上飘着的云。
glosses.en: yī xī yún: clouds drifting over a stream.

translation.zh: 清朗的夜晚，没有一点灰尘，
translation.en: The clear night is free of dust.
it must be filled to the brim.

translation.zh: 那些虚浮的名声和钱财，
只会让人白白受苦、耗费精神。
translation.en: only make you suffer for nothing and wear out your mind.

translation.zh: 可叹人生像白马跑过墙缝，
translation.en: Sadly, life is like a horse flashing past a crack in the wall,
like a spark struck from a stone,
like a body in a dream.
Though I am full of learning,

translation.zh: 说出心里话，又有谁来理解我？
translation.en: when I speak my mind, who will understand me?
For now, let me be happy

translation.zh: 尽情享受本来的真性情。
translation.en: and enjoy my true self to the full.
and be a man of leisure,

background.zh: “述怀”就是说说心里话。这首词的写作时间说法不一，多数人认为是苏轼在官场上不顺心的时候写的。那时他常常身不由己，在各地奔波，心里很想放下名利，回到家乡过自由自在的生活。他在月夜饮酒，把这些想法写了下来。
background.en: "Telling my heart" means saying what is really on your mind. People disagree about when this lyric was written. Most think Su Shi wrote it at a time when his official career was going badly. He was often sent from place to place without any say. He longed to put fame and money aside and go home to a free, easy life. Drinking on a moonlit night, he wrote these thoughts down.

author_note.zh: 苏轼（1037—1101），号东坡居士，北宋大文学家，诗、词、文章、书法、绘画样样精通。他一生几次被贬到远方，却总能乐观面对。他读过很多庄子的书，喜欢用庄子的道理看待人生的得失，这首词里就有这种味道。
author_note.en: Su Shi (1037–1101), also called Dongpo, was a great Northern Song writer. He excelled at poems, song lyrics, essays, calligraphy and painting. Several times he was sent away to distant posts, yet he always stayed cheerful. He read Zhuangzi a lot and liked to use its ideas to look at gains and losses in life. You can feel that in this lyric.

appreciation.zh: 开头是一幅干净的画：夜很清，月像银子，酒要倒满。接着话锋一转：名利都是虚的，只让人劳累。然后一口气用了三个比喻：墙缝里闪过的白马、石头上的火星、梦里的身影，都在说人生很短，像一下子就没了。下半首说自己有才华，却没人懂，那就先快活一点吧。最后的愿望很简单：一张琴，一壶酒，一溪云。三个“一”连在一起，读起来又轻松又悠长，好像人已经坐在溪边看云了。
appreciation.en: It opens with a clean picture: a clear night, moonlight like silver, wine poured to the brim. Then the tone turns. Fame and gain are empty and only wear you out. Next come three pictures in a row: a horse flashing past a crack, a spark from a stone, a figure in a dream. All say that life is short and gone in a moment. In the second half he says he has talent but nobody understands him, so for now he will just be happy. His last wish is simple: a zither, a pot of wine, a stream of clouds. The three "one"s in a row sound light and long, as if he is already sitting by the stream watching the clouds.
